- When sentiment is neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; correct by reducing forecast by 2–5% relative to peak or mean of recent history.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >95), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 90+), model should not continue upward trend; cap forecast at 10% below recent peak.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.25), model may overfit upward momentum; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% if sentiment is weak or fading.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day average to reduce lag error.
- If model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon (e.g., first 5 days), apply a 5–10% downward correction to first 3–5 forecast points.
